correctness.rationale: From continuous-time balance aπ1=(b+c)π2 and bπ2=cπ3 derive the displayed stationary vector. Differentiation yields the quartic F; its discriminant is −4r³P. Exact transformed coefficient sign counts, positive Bernstein coefficients and the all-positive translated expansion show P has one positive zero. Root-sign witnesses at r=0.01 and Descartes at r=1 fix root counts off this zero. The gcd of P with the cubic-discriminant factor excludes triple roots; hence the unique merger is a double root, and derivative signs give the 1-versus-2 maxima classification. Exact reflection D(r/x)−D(x) and F(sqrt r)>0 prove the smaller-rate local maximum is always the unique global maximum. The two-stage comparator proves minimality. The actual standalone Python verifier returned VERIFY_OK and checks finite rational algebra certificates, not infinite numerical enumeration.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The previous theory predicts possible two-peaked curves and attributes them to long-lived intermediate stages. The present theorem fixes one continuous-time three-stage reset generator and the Gini–Simpson stage index, determines an exact necessary-and-sufficient residence-time threshold, proves minimal stage count, and shows strict lower-disturbance global superiority for all rates. The qualitative claims do not specify which of the two peaks must be higher or where the exact algebraic bifurcation lies; conversely the present restricted theorem does not supersede their results for other indices, stage counts and spatial mechanisms.

residual_risks: The 2005 article notes Simpson diversity in its discussion, so the qualitative existence of bimodality is known, not novel. Its embedded equation images and all conceivable special cases have not been independently analyzed.

The 2007 Cadotte comparison was abstract-level, not a fully reviewed article body; its relation appears contextual rather than decisive.
No independent external scientific novelty assessment is represented.

value.rationale: The motivating 2005 study asked when successional disturbance-diversity curves possess one or two peaks. This result turns its residence-time mechanism into a sharp smallest-stage necessary-and-sufficient inequality, identifies the unique global optimizing disturbance rate despite local bistability of maxima, and gives a direct exact algebraic benchmark for Gini–Simpson stage diversity. It does not extrapolate to empirical preservation or other diversity indices. The sharp nontrivial threshold and ordering are mathematically substantive, not a routine reparameterization.
